class_name: 添加-非限定-ダケデナク類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Sets one item against a second on the same scale, the first understating the case and the second carrying it further, typically marked with まで or, under a negative, with も: スマホどころかタブレットまで使う, 旅行どころか外食もできない. The sibling lane is the reversal reading, where the second clause denies the first and states the opposite instead (効くどころかかえって熱が上がった, 反省どころか文句を言う). It attaches to a bare noun and to plain non-past forms; 〜たどころか is rare.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]はスマホどころかタブレットまで使[つか]いこなす。
examples.english: My grandmother doesn't just handle a smartphone, she's mastered a tablet too.

examples.ruby: その計画[けいかく]は難[むずか]しいどころか実現[じつげん]は不可能[ふかのう]に近[ちか]い。
examples.english: Calling that plan difficult is generous, pulling it off is next to impossible.

examples.ruby: 今月[こんげつ]は旅行[りょこう]どころか、外食[がいしょく]する余裕[よゆう]もない。
examples.english: This month I can't even afford to eat out, let alone take a trip.

patterns.usage_note: Piles a second property onto the first, with both pointing the same direction and describing the same subject (温泉がある上に朝食も豪華だ); mixing a good point with a complaint sounds off. It is the neutral "and what's more" of the group, without the counter-expectation of ばかりか. Plain non-past and past both attach, so 〜た上に is the normal way to stack up a run of misfortunes.

examples.ruby: この宿[やど]は温泉[おんせん]がある上[うえ]に朝食[ちょうしょく]も豪華[ごうか]だ。
examples.english: This inn has a hot spring, and the breakfast is lavish on top of that.

examples.ruby: あの店[みせ]は料理[りょうり]が出[で]てくるのが遅[おそ]い上[うえ]に値段[ねだん]も高[たか]い。
examples.english: At that place the food is slow to come out, and it's expensive on top of it.

examples.ruby: この自転車[じてんしゃ]は軽[かる]い上[うえ]に折[お]りたためるので、電車[でんしゃ]にも持[も]ち込[こ]める。
examples.english: This bike is light, and folds up besides, so you can even take it on the train.

patterns.usage_note: Adds a second item the listener would not have expected, so the following clause usually carries も or まで (眠気を誘うばかりか食欲まで奪う). It is more emphatic and more written than だけじゃなく but less stiff than のみならず, and unlike どころか it does not overturn the first item, it outdoes it. Nouns, plain non-past forms, and past 〜た all attach.

examples.ruby: この薬[くすり]は眠気[ねむけ]を誘[さそ]うばかりか食欲[しょくよく]まで奪[うば]う。
examples.english: This medicine doesn't just make you drowsy, it robs you of your appetite as well.

examples.ruby: あの人[ひと]は英語[えいご]ばかりかロシア語[ご]も話[はな]せる。
examples.english: That person speaks not only English but Russian as well.

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]は料理[りょうり]ができるばかりか包丁[ほうちょう]まで自分[じぶん]で研[と]ぐ。
examples.english: My brother can cook, and what's more he sharpens his own knives.

patterns.usage_note: Adds a second item in plain addition, without the counter-expectation of ばかりか or the evaluative jolt of どころか (雨だけじゃなく風も強い), and the second clause normally carries も or まで. だけじゃなく is the contracted spoken shape; だけでなく and だけではなく are the fuller written ones, and のみならず is the formal replacement. It attaches to nouns and plain forms.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]は雨[あめ]だけじゃなく風[かぜ]もすごく強[つよ]いよ。
examples.english: It's not just raining today, the wind is really howling too.

examples.ruby: あの先生[せんせい]は教[おし]えるだけじゃなく相談[そうだん]にも乗[の]ってくれる。
examples.english: That teacher doesn't just teach, he'll hear you out about your problems too.

examples.ruby: この靴[くつ]は軽[かる]いだけじゃなく雨[あめ]の日[ひ]でも滑[すべ]らない。
examples.english: These shoes aren't just light, they also grip on wet days.

patterns.usage_note: Adds a second item in formal written prose (国内のみならず海外でも), in reports, editorials, and speeches rather than conversation, with も or まで typically in the following clause. It is the formal counterpart of だけじゃなく; ばかりか marks counter-expectation, while のみならず is neutral enumeration. It also opens a sentence (のみならず、…) to attach a further point. Nouns, plain non-past, and 〜た attach.

examples.ruby: 当社[とうしゃ]は国内[こくない]のみならず海外[かいがい]でも事業[じぎょう]を広[ひろ]げている。
examples.english: The company is expanding its operations not only at home but abroad as well.

examples.ruby: 新[あら]たな制度[せいど]は学生[がくせい]を支[ささ]えるのみならず地域[ちいき]も潤[うるお]す。
examples.english: The new system not only supports students but enriches the surrounding community.

examples.ruby: その報告[ほうこく]は事実[じじつ]を誤認[ごにん]していたのみならず出典[しゅってん]も欠[か]いていた。
examples.english: The report not only got the facts wrong, it cited no sources either.
